recipe.title: Creamy White Bean Pumpkin Turkey Chili
recipe.summary: A smoky one-pot turkey chili with white beans, pumpkin, green chiles, Greek yogurt, and fresh jalapeños.
recipe.story: Pumpkin makes the broth thick and creamy without turning the chili sweet, while Kinder's Woodfired Chili Seasoning keeps the ingredient list short.
recipe.serving_size: 2 cups chili, 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt, and 1 tablespoon sliced jalapeños
ingredients: 2 cans (15 ounces each) Great Northern or cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (4 ounces) mild diced green chiles
4 cups Simple Truth Chicken Bone Broth, plus more only if needed
1 cup Chobani Nonfat Plain Greek Yogurt
instructions: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey and onion and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking the turkey apart, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F.
Sprinkle the Kinder's seasoning over the turkey and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the pumpkin and 1 cup bone broth. Stir until the pumpkin is smooth and fully incorporated.
Add the beans, green chiles, and remaining bone broth. Bring to a gentle boil, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Measure the finished chili. Continue simmering if the yield is more than 16 cups, or add a small amount of bone broth if needed, until the total batch equals 16 cups.
For each serving, ladle 2 cups chili into a bowl and top with 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt and 1 tablespoon thinly sliced jalapeños.
tips: The total batch must equal 16 cups for the listed serving size and macros.
Refrigerate the chili separately from the yogurt and jalapeños for up to four days.
Reheat each chili portion to 165°F before adding the cold toppings.
